claims.text: Cold deformation followed by moderate-temperature annealing will simultaneously improve yield strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance in high-entropy alloys.
The starting alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase FCC or BCC high-entropy alloy.
Cold deformation generates a high dislocation density.
Moderate-temperature annealing after cold deformation nucleates and preserves a uniform dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The proposed cold-deformation and annealing route creates a gradient microstructure.
Dislocations introduced by cold deformation provide nucleation sites for coherent precipitates during annealing.
Nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase yield strength.
The nanoscale coherent precipitates increase Young’s modulus.
A gradient microstructure enables deformation twinning or transformation-induced plasticity.
Deformation twinning and martensitic transformation can enhance work hardening and contribute to a favorable strength–ductility balance.
The gradient-enabled deformation modes preserve or enhance fracture resistance.
The proposed processing route will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed HEAs.
The proposed processing route will increase Young’s modulus by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed HEAs.
The proposed processing route will maintain or enhance ductility relative to a single-step route.
The proposed processing route will maintain or enhance fracture toughness relative to a single-step route.
Conventional strengthening of HEAs typically comes at the expense of ductility.
Precipitate coarsening will negate the expected mechanical-property improvements.
Formation of brittle intermetallic phases will reduce or negate the expected improvements, especially in ductility.
Unstable precipitate distributions or processing-induced stress concentrations can promote premature failure.
The nanoscale precipitate and gradient architectures may not remain stable during long-term service.
